pgtask

Run background tasks, schedules, and durable workflows with PostgreSQL as the only service you need.
Your first taskHow it works

pgtask stores tasks in your database and runs them from your own processes. There is no broker, no coordinator, and no PostgreSQL extension.

You enqueue a task in the same transaction that writes your application data. If the transaction rolls back, the task never existed. That single property removes most of the consistency problems that queues usually introduce.

One dependency

PostgreSQL owns every durable transition. Workers are ordinary processes you deploy and scale yourself.

Leases, not acknowledgements

A worker holds a fenced lease while it runs your handler. If it disappears, the task returns automatically.

Durable workflows

Steps, sleeps, signals, and child tasks are database transitions, so a workflow survives a process restart.

One protocol, many languages

Rust, Python, TypeScript, Go, and plain SQL speak the same versioned set of database functions.

Not ready for production

pgtask is under active development. The contracts described here are still changing.
